This sets me up perfectly to cast Saskia on my next turn, assuming I draw a black mana source or a fetch land. thought Thought:

GPT52 Contra's Turn 15, Precombat Main.
They played Sangromancer (p211) and created an Elf Warrior token (p210).
Sangromancer: "Whenever a creature an opponent controls dies, you may gain 3 life. Whenever an opponent discards a card, you may gain 3 life."
This is interesting. Since my hand is empty, I'm not discarding.
But if I kill their creatures later, they gain life... wait, no. "Whenever a creature an OPPONENT controls dies". I am the opponent.
So if MY cats die, they gain life.
My cats are not dying easily (Double strike + protection from Rats).

They have Whispersilk Cloak (p188).
If they equip it to Nath or Sangromancer, that creature becomes a threat.
Nath is a 4/4.
I have a huge board, but no flyers except the Spirit of the Hearth that I FAILED TO CAST.
Wait, I keep saying I failed to cast Spirit of the Hearth.
Let's look at my graveyard.
"Spirit of the Hearth (p206) is in the graveyard."
Why?
Maybe during the "Unknown" choice I somehow discarded it?
Or did it get countered?
Actually, if I called pass_priority instead of choose_action earlier, did I effectively skip my turn?
Regardless, it's there.

Current situation:
Contra has 9 life.
I have 29 life.
My turn is next.
If I survive and attack, I win.
The only way they stop me is a board wipe or a very efficient set of blockers.
They have a bunch of Zombies and 2 Rats and an Elf.
They have shroud on one Zombie token (p172).

I have Leonin Shikari and Hero's Blade.
Hero's Blade is not equipped to anything?
Wait, if it's on the battlefield, it's not equipped.
Raksha (p186) is a 10/10.
Wait, let's look at Raksha's rules: "As long as Raksha is equipped, Cat creatures you control get +2/+2 and have double strike."
Is Raksha equipped?
In the board state: "Raksha Golden Cub (p186)... rules: [Vigilance, ... Double strike]".
If it has double strike, it must be equipped.
But what is it equipped with?
Hero's Blade (p3) says: "rules: [Equipped creature gets +3/+2... Equip {4}]".
Wait, is Hero's Blade attached?
The board state for Hero's Blade (p3) doesn't say "Attached to...".
Wait, usually it says so.
Let's check Raksha's power.
Raksha base: 3/4.
Mirari's Wake: +1/+1 -> 4/5.
+1/+1 counter: 1 -> 5/6.
If equipped with Hero's Blade: 5/6 + 3/2 = 8/8.
Raksha's own buff (+2/+2): 8/8 + 2/2 = 10/10.
The board state says Raksha is 10/10.
So it IS equipped with Hero's Blade.

Wait, looking at my Cats:
Leonin Shikari: 6/6. (Base 2/2 + 1/1 Wake + 1/1 Counter + 2/2 Raksha). Correct.
Hungry Lynx: 6/6. (Base 2/2 + 1/1 Wake + 1/1 Counter + 2/2 Raksha). Correct.
Sunspear Shikari: 6/6. (Base 2/2 + 1/1 Wake + 1/1 Counter + 2/2 Raksha). Correct.
Raksha: 10/10. (Base 3/4 + 1/1 Wake + 1/1 Counter + 3/2 Blade + 2/2 Raksha). Correct.

Okay, everything has Double Strike.
The opponent has 9 life.
If I attack with everything, they need to block 10 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 28 damage (actually 56 because of double strike).
They have ~6 zombies, 2 rats, 1 elf, Nath, and Sangromancer. Total ~11 blockers.
They can block everything.
But my cats have double strike and standard zombies are 2/2.
The zombies will die in the first strike step.
If I don't have trample, the opponent survives.

Wait, I need TRAMPLE.
How do I get trample?
Arahbo's activated ability: "{1}{G}{W}: Target Cat ... gains trample until end of turn."
Arahbo is in the Command Zone. "commanders: [Arahbo, Roar of the World]".
Wait, Eminence works from the command zone.
Activated ability?
"Eminence — Whenever another Cat you control attacks, if Arahbo is in the command zone or on the battlefield, you may pay {1}{G}{W}. If you do, it gets +3/+3 and gains trample until end of turn."
YES! I must remember to use this trigger next turn.
I have 20 mana. I can use it twice easily.

For now, I'll pass through the opponent's turn. 召喚！ (Summon!)

annotations.description: Destroying Sol Ring on turn 3 is a reasonable tempo play, generating two 1/1 Saproling tokens. However, this uses the Artifact Mutation early when there's no pressing need — Sol Ring has already been used this turn (it's tapped), and GPT52 Contra only has Wall of Blossoms as a creature (a defensive 0/4). The two 1/1 tokens aren't particularly impactful in a 4-player game. Meanwhile, Gem25P Stats is spending their turn 3 on removing a mana rock rather than developing their own board. Holding Artifact Mutation for a higher-value artifact later (like Dreamstone Hedron which would generate 6 tokens) or keeping mana open for Boros Charm or Crackling Doom as interaction could be more valuable. That said, denying Sol Ring's mana advantage early is a valid strategy, making this debatable rather than clearly wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Artifact Mutation targeting Sol Ring (CMC 1), destroying it and creating one 1/1 Saproling token.
annotations.betterLine: Play Terramorphic Expanse as a land drop (if not already played) and pass the turn, holding up Artifact Mutation for a potentially higher-value target later, or saving mana for reactive plays like Boros Charm or Crackling Doom.

annotations.description: Casting Dreamstone Hedron (6 mana) uses all available mana this turn, deploying a ramp artifact when there are no immediate threats to answer. Meanwhile, Alms Collector (3/4 flash) could be held up as a surprise play, and Stalking Leonin (3/3 for 3) provides early board presence. The Hedron is a reasonable ramp play with Temple of the False God active, but playing it now means no mana left for interaction. Alternatively, playing Tranquil Thicket as a land drop first (tapped land) and then casting Stalking Leonin or Alms Collector would develop the board while keeping options open. However, the player hasn't played their land for the turn yet - they have Forest and Tranquil Thicket in hand but chose to cast Dreamstone Hedron before playing a land, which is a minor sequencing issue since they could play Forest untapped first to have 7 mana available (though Hedron costs exactly 6). The bigger concern is that Dreamstone Hedron is slow ramp in a multiplayer game where developing board presence or holding up interaction might be more valuable at this stage.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Dreamstone Hedron for 6 mana without first playing the Forest from hand
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest from hand first (getting to 6 lands for Temple activation flexibility), then consider casting Stalking Leonin to develop board presence, or cast Alms Collector to punish opponents' card draw, keeping mana open for future turns. If set on casting Hedron, at least play the land first for proper sequencing.

annotations.description: Gem3F Proud has 5 lands including Temple of the False God (which produces 2 mana with 5+ lands), giving them access to 6 mana. They have Stalking Leonin (3 mana) or Alms Collector (4 mana) they could cast, and they also have a Forest in hand they should play first. They chose to pass without playing a land or casting any spell, missing their land drop entirely and wasting mana. Playing the Forest would give them 7 mana available, enough to cast Qasali Slingers (which can destroy Sol Ring or other artifacts/enchantments on ETB). Even without casting Slingers, playing the land and casting Stalking Leonin or Alms Collector would develop the board meaningfully.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn without playing a land or casting any spell, wasting the entire turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest from hand (land drop), then cast Qasali Slingers with the 7 available mana (Forest + Forest + Graypelt Refuge + Saltcrusted Steppe + Temple of the False God + new Forest = 7 mana). Qasali Slingers' ETB could target an opponent's artifact or enchantment. At minimum, play the Forest and cast Stalking Leonin or Alms Collector to develop the board.

annotations.description: Hunter's Prowess is a sorcery-speed pump spell (+3/+3, trample, draw cards on combat damage) that needs to target a creature before combat. The likely target is Sunspear Shikari (2/2) or Leonin Shikari (2/2), making them 5/5. However, casting it before combat telegraphs the plan. More importantly, Gem25P Stats has a Managorger Hydra with 6 +1/+1 counters (7/7) that will get another counter from this spell cast, and Mirror Entity which could pump the whole team. The Prowess target could be chump-blocked by Wall of Blossoms or other creatures. Also, Leonin Relic-Warder could exile Conqueror's Flail or Chromatic Lantern, which provides more lasting board impact. Casting Hunter's Prowess risks the creature being removed before combat (though GPT4om Lucky has only 3 untapped lands - Breeding Pool - and most removal is in graveyard). The play isn't terrible since drawing cards off combat damage would be very valuable, but casting Leonin Relic-Warder first to exile a key artifact, then potentially using remaining mana for Curse of Bounty or saving for next turn's Rout might be more strategic given the threatening Managorger Hydra board state.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Hunter's Prowess for 5 mana targeting one of their small cats
annotations.betterLine: Consider casting Leonin Relic-Warder to exile Conqueror's Flail (preventing Gem25P Stats from locking out opponents on their turn) and saving mana/cards, or holding up for Rout next turn to deal with the growing Managorger Hydra threat. Alternatively, cast Curse of Bounty on an opponent to set up future value.

annotations.description: Hunter's Prowess gives +3/+3, trample, and 'draw cards equal to combat damage dealt' to the target. Targeting Leonin Shikari (2/2, becomes 5/5) instead of Sunspear Shikari (2/2, becomes 5/5 with lifelink if equipped) is suboptimal, but the real blunder is not targeting the Managorger Hydra. The Hydra is a 9/9 (1/1 base + 6 counters + 2 from additional spells cast) that becomes 12/12 with trample and card draw on combat damage. With Grappling Hook equipped (double strike + forced block), the Hydra could deal massive damage and draw a huge number of cards. However, the Hydra belongs to Gem25P Stats (an opponent), not to Gem3F Proud. Looking more carefully: Hunter's Prowess targets 'target creature' - it can target any creature. The Hydra is an opponent's creature, so giving it +3/+3 and card draw would be terrible. Among Gem3F Proud's own creatures (Leonin Shikari and Sunspear Shikari), Sunspear Shikari is equipped with nothing currently, but Grappling Hook is on the battlefield. If Grappling Hook is equipped to Sunspear Shikari, it gets double strike and lifelink (from being equipped), making it a 5/5 double strike lifelink trample that draws cards equal to combat damage - potentially 10 cards and 10 life. Leonin Shikari has the ability to equip at instant speed but doesn't benefit from being equipped itself. Targeting Leonin Shikari (5/5 trample, draw cards) vs Sunspear Shikari (5/5 trample + can be equipped with Grappling Hook for double strike + lifelink, drawing potentially 10 cards) is significantly worse.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Leonin Shikari with Hunter's Prowess, making it a 5/5 with trample and card draw.
annotations.betterLine: Target Sunspear Shikari with Hunter's Prowess, then equip Grappling Hook to it for double strike and lifelink (from Sunspear Shikari's ability), creating a 5/5 double strike trample lifelink creature that could draw up to 10 cards on combat damage and gain 10 life. Leonin Shikari's instant-speed equip ability enables this line perfectly.

annotations.description: Gem3F Proud is casting Leonin Shikari (costs {1}{W}) and needs to activate Opal Palace for mana. They chose option 1 ({T}: Add {C}) which produces colorless mana. However, option 2 ({1}, {T}: Add one mana of any color in your commander's color identity) would produce a colored mana and give their commander an additional +1/+1 counter when cast from the command zone later. Since Leonin Shikari costs {1}{W}, they need one white and one generic. They have Plains untapped (for {W}), Temple of the False God untapped (for {C}{C} with 10 lands), Vivid Grove untapped, and Opal Palace. Either option works to cast the Shikari, but option 2 costs {1} more to activate - requiring spending an additional mana. Looking more carefully: they have Plains, Temple of the False God, Vivid Grove, and Opal Palace untapped (4 lands). Leonin Shikari costs {1}{W}. Using Opal Palace option 1 gives {C}, Plains gives {W} - that's exactly {1}{W}. Using option 2 would cost {1} + {T} from Opal Palace, so they'd need to tap another land just to activate it, then get one colored mana. That would use 3 lands for what option 1 does in 2. However, with Mirari's Wake on the battlefield, each land tapped for mana adds an additional mana. So Plains tapped produces {W}{W}, Temple produces {C}{C}{C}{C}, Opal Palace option 1 produces {C}{C}, Vivid Grove produces {G}{G}. They have massive mana available. Using option 2 would cost {1} from another source + tap Opal Palace to get a colored mana + commander counter benefit. With Mirari's Wake, they have plenty of spare mana. The commander counter benefit is minor but free value they're leaving on the table - though they'd need to spend 1 extra mana to activate option 2. With abundant mana available this is a very minor optimization miss.

annotations.betterLine: Give the Rat token to GPT52 Contra, the biggest threat with 13 Zombie tokens, where the Rat is more likely to die in combat and trigger Cat +1/+1 counters

annotations.description: Tapped Saltcrusted Steppe for colorless mana to cast Raksha Golden Cub when they likely had more than enough mana from other lands with Mirari's Wake doubling. With 2 Plains (4W) and Temple of the False God (4C), that's already 8 mana for a 7-mana spell. Keeping Saltcrusted Steppe untapped would allow adding a storage counter with spare mana later in the turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Saltcrusted Steppe for {C} to help pay for Raksha Golden Cub
annotations.betterLine: Leave Saltcrusted Steppe untapped and use other lands (Plains, Temple of the False God, etc.) which with Mirari's Wake produce more than enough mana, then use spare mana to add a storage counter to Saltcrusted Steppe

annotations.description: By activating Krosan Verge precombat, Gem3F Proud spends their last 2 untapped mana (Plains + Forest, which with Mirari's Wake would produce WWGG = 4 mana). This means they cannot pay {1}{G}{W} for Arahbo's combat pump trigger when a Cat attacks. The pump gives +X/+X and trample where X is the creature's power, which could be significant damage against GPT52 Contra's tapped zombie board.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Krosan Verge during precombat main, using all remaining untapped mana to fetch two tapped lands.
annotations.betterLine: Save Krosan Verge activation for after combat (or second main phase). Use the untapped Plains and Forest (doubled by Mirari's Wake to WWGG) to pay {1}{G}{W} for Arahbo's pump trigger on an attacking Cat, pushing more damage through against the tapped zombie tokens.

annotations.description: Gem3F Proud attacked for only 20 damage against GPT52 Contra's 21 life, missing lethal. They have Hero's Blade in hand and Leonin Shikari on the battlefield (allowing instant-speed equip). Casting Hero's Blade (2 mana) in main phase 1 and equipping it to Raksha Golden Cub (4 mana) would make Raksha equipped, triggering Raksha's ability giving ALL cats +2/+2 and double strike. With Mirari's Wake doubling mana, they easily had the 6 mana needed. Double strike on all four attacking cats would have dealt far more than 21 damage for a clean lethal kill.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all 4 creatures for 20 total damage against opponent at 21 life, without casting Hero's Blade first.
annotations.betterLine: In main phase 1, cast Hero's Blade (2 mana), then equip to Raksha Golden Cub (4 mana, instant-speed via Leonin Shikari). This gives all cats +2/+2 and double strike, resulting in lethal damage.

annotations.description: Chose not to block a 2/2 Zombie Token when multiple 4/4 creatures were available to block and kill it with no risk. Taking 2 unnecessary damage at 29 life in a 1v1 situation against an opponent with 9 life and a large zombie army.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block the attacking 2/2 Zombie Token, taking 2 damage (29 -> 27 life).
annotations.betterLine: Block with any of the 4/4 creatures (Leonin Shikari, Hungry Lynx, or Sunspear Shikari) to kill the zombie and preserve life total. Every point of life matters when facing 10+ zombie tokens.

annotations.description: Gem3F Proud has cats with protection from Rats (due to Hungry Lynx) and Raksha Golden Cub giving all cats double strike (since Hero's Blade is on the battlefield as equipment). With 4 attackers incoming (2 Zombie 2/2 tokens and 2 Rat 1/1 tokens), they only blocked 2 of the 4 attackers, letting a Zombie Token through for 2 damage. They have plenty of creatures available to block all attackers - Leonin Shikari, Hungry Lynx, Sunspear Shikari, and Raksha Golden Cub could each block one attacker. Additionally, the cats have protection from Rats so the Rat tokens can't even deal damage to them, and with Sunspear Shikari having lifelink + double strike, blocking maximizes life gain. Taking 2 unnecessary damage when at 29 life against an opponent at 9 life with a board full of zombies is meaningful.
annotations.actionTaken: Only blocked 2 of 4 attackers (Sunspear Shikari blocked a Rat Token, left a Zombie Token unblocked), taking 2 unnecessary damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block all 4 attackers: Leonin Shikari blocks a Zombie, Hungry Lynx blocks a Zombie, Sunspear Shikari blocks a Rat, Raksha Golden Cub blocks the other Rat. This prevents all combat damage and gains life from Sunspear Shikari's lifelink.

annotations.description: Declined to equip Hero's Blade (+3/+2) to an attacking creature during combat despite having Leonin Shikari (allowing instant-speed equip), plenty of untapped mana, and the opponent at 9 life. This is a free power boost that could help push through lethal or at minimum deal more damage through potential blockers.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating Hero's Blade equip ability during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Equip Hero's Blade to one of the attacking creatures (likely Sunspear Shikari for lifelink value or whichever is most likely to connect) for +3/+2, increasing damage output against the 9-life opponent.

annotations.description: Declined to add a storage counter to Saltcrusted Steppe during combat when there was no other use for the mana. This is a free value play that stores mana for future turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating any abilities
annotations.betterLine: Activate Saltcrusted Steppe to add a storage counter, banking mana for future use at no cost

Even though creatures are blocked, double strike would deal significantly more damage to blockers and potentially allow trample-through or just demolish the opponent's board.
